questions.q: What is the main idea of the essay?
options: Meetings are a waste of time and should be abolished entirely
Founders should keep wearing jeans instead of switching to suits
Managers and makers use time differently, so meetings cost makers far more
Investors should hold office hours every morning to meet founders
questions.explain: The author contrasts the manager's hourly schedule with the maker's half-day units, where a meeting is a disaster.

questions.q: How does the author say a manager's schedule is divided by default?
options: Into half-day units
Into one-hour intervals
Into fifteen-minute slots
Into week-long projects
questions.explain: The appointment book cuts each day into one hour intervals, and you change what you do every hour by default.

questions.q: How does the author keep office hours from interrupting his workday?
options: He holds them only on Fridays, when no programming is planned
He lets founders book any slot they like, mixing them into his day
He cancels them whenever a coding project hits a busy stretch
He clusters them at the end of his day using a signup program
questions.explain: He sets office hours at the end of the day and wrote a signup program to cluster appointments there.

questions.q: What are the two options when someone proposes a speculative meeting to a maker?
options: Meet and lose half a day, or decline and probably offend them
Meet by phone briefly, or meet over lunch to save time
Delegate it to Jessica, or postpone it for a whole year
Hold it as office hours, or answer with a short email
questions.explain: The author says they can meet and lose half a day's work, or avoid meeting and probably offend them.

questions.q: Why does the author describe a meeting as 'throwing an exception' for a maker?
options: It makes the maker forget which task was meant to come next
It forces a change in the mode of work, not just a switch of tasks
It signals an error caused by poor planning on the maker's part
It permanently ends the project the maker was working on that day
questions.explain: The passage says a meeting does not merely switch tasks; it changes the mode in which you work.
